primary_claim: A prototype 'natural language transcoder' that verbalizes and reconstructs the delta between a transformer's embedding and final-layer residual streams improves substantially from SFT warm-start to joint RL training on Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, raising raw-delta fraction of variance explained from 0.119 to 0.503 and target-model top-1 next-token agreement from 11.9% to 29.5%, though a manual audit of 100 explanations found only 20% were both contextually plausible and correct about which tokens were promoted/suppressed

effect.metric: raw-delta fraction of variance explained (FVE); delta cosine similarity; target-model top-1/top-5 next-token agreement; audit correctness on 100 sampled explanations
effect.value: Raw-delta FVE: 0.119 -> 0.503; Delta cosine: 0.667 -> 0.818; top-1 agreement: 11.9% -> 29.5%; top-5 overlap: 18.2% -> 39.6% (SFT vs after RL); audit: 20/100 both contextually plausible and token-correct

stated_future_work: repeat the experiment using a 7B model as the base model for the AV and AR, e.g. Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct
limitations_stated: struggles with partial tokens, BPE fragments, dates, timestamps, and numbers where exact continuation is required
frequently detects the general domain but names the wrong specific entity or subdomain
sometimes calls a token promoted because it appears in final top candidates even when its actual logit change is negative
produces unstable explanations for noisy or composite text (forum metadata, malformed web text, concatenated pages)
because the AV receives only the delta without the original prefix, it can recover coarse information but not which specific noun, number, entity, or event is intended
